title: Will there be more than 170 transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Oct 26, 2026 to Nov 1, 2026? Above 170
rules: If the number of transit calls through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 170 from Oct 26, 2026 to Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: The total is calculated by summing daily counts from Oct 26, 2026 to Nov 1, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

blind.reasoning: IMF PortWatch's most recently published week (Oct 5-11, 2026) averaged about 28 Bab el-Mandeb transits a day, roughly 196 a week, against a threshold of 170 (about 24.3 a day). An Oct 25 UKMTO report said traffic was holding steady, but the cushion is only about 13%. Weekly counts are noisy, and Houthi escalation (Mayyun Island occupation, strikes on Saudi Arabia, attacks on Saudi-linked ships) could cut traffic further.
blind.falsifier: PortWatch daily counts for Oct 26-Nov 1, 2026 averaging 24 or fewer a day, for example after a new Houthi attack on merchant shipping that prompts carriers to suspend transits.

final.reasoning: The 0.865 midpoint likely reflects recent weekly PortWatch data (Oct 12-25) that I couldn't see, so I moved up from 0.70 toward it. My remaining discount for Houthi escalation risk is too small an edge to bet NO against a market that may know more.
